links.comparator_used: Same fine-tuned backbones without the density-aware focal loss (baseline loss), ablated across three auxiliary weights
links.effect: Density-aware focal loss degraded both AUC and calibration at every one of the three auxiliary weights tested (no specific numbers given in the abstract)
links.quote: The density-aware focal loss degraded both AUC and calibration at every weight tested.

links.comparator_used: ResNet-50 (standard general-purpose backbone) and general-purpose DINOv2-B14, versus mammography/radiology-specific models (Rad-DINO, Mammo-CLIP B5, Mammo-FM)
links.outcome: AUC in-distribution (CBIS-DDSM) and at external transfer cohorts (CMMD, DMID, MIAS)
links.effect: In-distribution ResNet-50 AUC 0.867 vs 0.847, 0.846, 0.813, 0.703 for the four foundation models (all p_adj < 0.05). At transfer, Mammo-CLIP B5 and Mammo-FM significantly outperformed ResNet-50 on DMID and Mammo-CLIP on CMMD after BH-FDR; MIAS directional only. In the BI-RADS D4 subgroup, Mammo-FM AUC 0.870 vs ResNet-50 0.842 (CIs overlap, not statistically supported).
links.tradeoff: Every model lost 0.165 to 0.320 AUC points at transfer; sensitivity at 95% specificity fell from 0.31-0.47 to 0.11-0.22, so none was defensible for deployment without local validation.
links.quote: Within this single-source three-seed evaluation, ResNet-50 outperformed all four foundation models on CBIS-DDSM (AUC 0.867 vs. 0.847, 0.846, 0.813, and 0.703; all gaps p_adj < 0.05).

design_hint: local recalibration (temperature scaling) and external validation before deployment
